Priyanka S.: Hey team — a weird one. I rented a car in Boston for client visits. The rental charged me $78.40 at pickup on the corp card, but I just got a separate "TOLL MANAGEMENT SERVICE" charge for $18.50 three days later from a third-party aggregator. I don't have a paper toll receipt. How do I submit/claim this? The rental company's folio only shows vehicle + insurance, not the toll.
Oliver (Finance): Thanks for raising. For third-party toll aggregator charges, we need: 1) the rental folio; 2) the aggregator email/transaction id (usually in your email); 3) a short note explaining why tolls are business (client drive routes). If the corp card was charged for the aggregator, we won't reimburse. If you paid personally, we can reimburse. Which card posted the $18.50?
Priyanka S.: The aggregator charge posted to the corp card (card ending 7789) on 2025-05-12 and the description is "TOLL MGR SVCS US". I have the aggregator email with TXN-AG-5521 and a screenshot of the card line in the banking app. Uploaded: rental_folio.pdf -> https://redwood-files/receipts/rental_1751239876.pdf ; toll_email.pdf -> https://redwood-files/receipts/toll_email_1751239876.pdf ; cardline.png -> https://redwood-files/receipts/cardline_1751239876.png
expense-bot: For tolls billed by a third party to the corporate card, create a reconciliation note via the expenses tool: ```/expenses reconcile --card 7789 --tx 1751239876 --attach toll_email.pdf,rental_folio.pdf,cardline.png --notes "Third-party toll aggregator charge posted after rental; request reconciliation with rental agency for itemization"```
Marta L.: FYI some rental agencies bill tolls to the card and then contract a third party to collect later. Finance policy: if the toll is legitimate business usage and posted to the corporate card, we keep it on the corp ledger. If the toll was charged in error (e.g., private use) or is a fee for a GPS device, we'll investigate with the vendor.
Oliver (Finance): We'll open a vendor inquiry with the rental company to get itemized toll details and the aggregator's remittance report. Priyanka, thanks for attaching the emails. If the aggregator is charging an extra service fee (e.g., per-transaction processing), we may ask the vendor to absorb that or we can treat the processing fee as admin under $20 and absorb it.
Priyanka S.: The aggregator's email shows breakdown: tolls $15.00 + processing fee $3.50 = $18.50. If the $15 corresponds to route tolls for client visits, I agree that's business. Can finance absorb the $3.50 processing fee?
Oliver (Finance): For processing fees under $5 tied to third-party toll reconciliation we typically absorb them once per incident. We'll confirm after we get the itemized remittance from the aggregator. We'll also match the toll timestamps to your rental period.
Marta L.: I'll kick off the vendor outreach and cc you. If the rental vendor refuses to provide itemization, we'll keep the toll but tag it as "vendor unverified tolls" and mark for periodic audit.
corp-card-bot: Charge matched to cardline. Status: under-investigation -> /expenses view 1751239876
Priyanka S.: Appreciate it — ping me if you need my rental contract number. It's RNT-33211.
Oliver (Finance): Noted. I'll update here when vendor replies. Expected turnaround 3-5 business days. Thanks for the complete attachments.
Priyanka S.: Thanks! Will wait for the update.
